newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Apr 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Apr 11.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- The Immigration Department plans to deport a total of 1,200 child illegal immigrants to China to shoot down rumours that there would be an amnesty for illegal immigrants.

-- SING TAO DAILY -- The Hong Kong government said it opposed proposals by the Chief Executive-designate's office to introduce the concept of national security in deciding whether to ban or restrict social organisations and demonstrations.
-- A technician was killed by shrapnel from a controlled explosion when a movie company was filming a stunt in Sek Kong.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese vice premier Li Langqing said China's foreign trade figure was forecast at US$310 billion, up seven percent from 1996.
-- WEN WEI PO -- Hong Kong's Western Harbour Crossing will open for traffic on April 30 and operation of the Tsing Yi-Lantau Island expressway is schedule to start on May 22.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Chairman Anthony Neoh of the Securities and Futures Commission said he would hold talks with the chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission during the International Organisation of Securities Commissions meeting in Beijing next week.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- The Hong Kong Housing Society will sell 228 units in its residential property development in Kowloon at a market price of about HK$5,986 per square foot.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The government issued a commentary warning legislative changes published by the Chief Executive-designate's Office would significantly increase offical powers to restrict freedom of assembly and association.
-- The Guangdong Supreme People's Court was expected to hand down verdicts soon on two unionists, Li Wenming and Guo Baosheng, charged with subversion, San Francisco-based lobbyist John Kamm said.
